model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the relationship between coverage and the number of completions (k) for four different Llama model configurations: Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k),” uses a logarithmic scale ranging from 2⁰ (1) to 2⁸ (256), with major tick marks at each power of two. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” is linear and spans from 0.4 to 0.8, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. The Llama-3B line (solid blue with circular markers) starts at approximately 0.43 at k=1 and rises steadily to about 0.88 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT line (solid green with triangular markers) begins slightly lower at ~0.42 and increases to ~0.86 at k=256, tracking closely below Llama-3B. The Llama-1B line (solid light blue with circular markers) starts at ~0.31 and climbs to ~0.82. The Llama-1B + FT line (solid light green with triangular markers) begins at ~0.30 and reaches ~0.80 at k=256, remaining consistently below the Llama-1B line. All lines exhibit a concave-upward trend, indicating diminishing returns in coverage gain as k increases.
